To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transferability of a generic ConvNet representation is affected by several factors and by optimizing them, significant improvements in transferability can be achieved.

the factors that affect the performance of a target task when a ConvNet is used as a source for transfer learning are: (1) the architecture of the source ConvNets, (2) the distribution of the training set, (3) the dimensionality of the extracted features, and (4) the layer of the source ConvNe t at which the extracted features are obtained.

the performance of the target tasks can be significantly improved by: (1) training a source ConvNet with a larger training set and a more complex architecture, (2) extracting the representation from a deeper layer, (3) reducing the dimension of the extracted features, and (4) using a ConvNet with a smaller number of layers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: what are the key parameters that determine the performance of transfer learning using ConvNets?
a better understanding of the factors that affect the transferability of ConvNet representations.
the following question: "How to best utilize a ConvNet for representation transfer?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a good representation for a target task can be learned using a trained ConvNet on a source task, if and only if, the source task is similar enough to the target task w.r.t the proposed factors.
the performance of a target task is directly proportional to its similarity to the source in terms of the proposed factors.
the proposed factors can be used for categorizing the target tasks into different levels of transferability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a set of factors that can be used to measure similarity between visual recognition tasks and we also show how this similarity can be exploited in the context of representation transfer.
we show how to improve the transferability of ConvNets and also that we show how ConvNet representations are more transferable to similar tasks than dissimilar tasks.
we show that the transferability of a ConvNet representation is not a binary decision, i.e. either it works or it does not.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a generic representation transfer from a ConvNet trained on a large source task to a target task with smaller amount of training data is possible, and that the performance of such a transfer is highly affected by the parameters of the source Convnet and the parameters of feature representation extraction.
the performance of the transfer learning approach is highly dependent on the factors we propose and can be significantly improved by optimizing these factors.
a ConvNet can be used as a generic image representation, and its performance on various visual recognition tasks can significantly be improved by optimizing the factors affecting its transferability.
